historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun describes him as a learned man and a patron of scholars. He extended the boundaries of the Marinid empire and is known for his justice and fairness.

historical_references.reference: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ahidas was a prominent Sufi master in the 15th century in the city of Tlemcen, Algeria. He was a disciple of the famous Sufi master, Ibn Ata Allah of Rabat. Ahida is known for his teachings on love and self-annihilation in the path of God.
historical_references.context: Ahida's teachings have been influential among Sufis in North Africa and beyond.
